evidence.why: Signature, base/working severity and vector calculation.
Candidate motion, ice exception and facing override.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unconditional motion-override claim and distinguishes facing presentation from the already calculated launch vector.
facts.value: Side-effect-only damage initializer with signature void(Fighter_GObj*, int motion_override, float facing_override). Motion override -1 requests automatic selection; another value forces the working severity to 3 and supplies a candidate motion, but base-severity-at-least-2 ice damage can replace that candidate with numeric 0x5A unless it is 0x145. A zero facing override keeps hit-derived facing; a nonzero value replaces it after launch-vector calculation.

evidence.why: Complete ordered initialization and final ice handling.

facts.rationale: Corrects movement-clear ordering and preserves the zero-only countdown adjustment, distinct severity values and exceptional ice branches.
facts.value: Entry truncates applied knockback times x154 into damage.x0 and replaces a zero result with one. It retains a base severity for ice behavior while an explicit motion request forces the working severity to 3. Ground/air geometry and optional airborne eligibility scaling determine launch velocity. Ordinary self velocity and ground velocity are cleared before motion entry. Automatic strong-airborne motion selection and caller motion selection are followed by the ice override, except for numeric 0x145. After motion entry it installs hitlag callbacks, resets input and damage timers, sets the active damage flag and initializes feedback; the final DamageIce initializer is skipped for motion 0x145 and base severity below 2.

evidence.why: Cooldown handling followed by DamageSong-versus-common-entry dispatch.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes the wrapper's exclusive reaction dispatch from the lower-level initializer and resolves the rendered ftCo_Damage_Enter collision without asserting historical spelling.

evidence.why: Exact numeric element and exclusion guards.
Variant-sensitive duration, state entry and mash processing.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported sleep mechanic while removing unsupported attacker-specific exclusivity and making the numeric variant mapping explicit.
facts.value: Dispatches the victim's resolved hit into a sleep-family DamageSong reaction or ordinary damage initialization. Numeric elements 6 and 7 select DamageSong when x2228_b2 is clear, passing timer-variant arguments 0 and 1 respectively. DamageSong initializes a mash-sensitive duration. This dispatcher does not inspect attacker identity, so the two element cases should not both be identified exclusively with Jigglypuff's Sing from this evidence.

facts.rationale: Separates the exact local call contract from exceptional state choices in the delegated fallback.
facts.value: Side-effect-only ground-impact dispatcher void(Fighter_GObj*). It returns immediately after either Boolean tech predicate succeeds; otherwise it unconditionally invokes ftCo_80097D40. That fallback is a DownBound-family dispatcher, not a guarantee that the final motion is DownBound.

evidence.why: Ordinary and exceptional fallback paths, followed by x4 reset.

facts.rationale: Preserves recovery priority and the post-call field reset while documenting the cross-file exception to guaranteed DownBound entry.
facts.value: Attempts directional PassiveStand recovery first, then the shared-gate neutral recovery, stopping on the first success. If both fail it calls ftCo_80097D40, which clears downspot.x4 after delegated handling. The ordinary fallback enters DownBoundU/D; with x2228_b2 set, the delegated helper also examines model orientation and can instead call grounded neutral handling or ftSb_Init_8014FBA4. A missed tech therefore guarantees fallback invocation, not a particular final motion.

evidence.why: Meteor guards, snapshot and buffer consumer.

facts.rationale: Corrects the conflation of the demonstrated jump-buffer snapshot with anti-mashing penalties while preserving meteor-cancel and post-hitstun behavior.
facts.value: Selects between restricted damage-flight input handling during active hitstun and DamageFall's actionable tumbling inputs afterward. The restricted helper can perform an eligible meteor cancel and otherwise records jump input by snapshotting the remaining damage countdown. That local snapshot is jump-buffer bookkeeping; it is not itself an anti-mashing penalty timer.

evidence.why: Complete restricted helper and ordinary IASA consumer.

facts.rationale: Replaces ambiguous timer-like wording with the exact snapshot assignment and nonzero-and-less-than-or-equal consumer guard.
facts.value: While x221C_b6 is set, delegates only to doIasa: its meteor path requires the enable flag, expired delay, airborne downward knockback and a successful up-special or aerial-jump predicate; otherwise qualifying jump input copies the current damage.x0 into damage.x14. After the active flag clears, Hammer carriers use HammerFall or HammerWait IASA according to situation. Other fighters synthesize XY input only when the stored x14 snapshot is nonzero and no greater than x1D0, then run Fall IASA in air or Wait IASA on ground. This callback does not decrement x14 or wait for it to reach a threshold.
